newsitem.title: USA: Check Technology sees lower Q1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Check Technology sees lower Q1 earnings.

text.p: Check Technology Corp said Monday it expects earnings for the first quarter of nil to $0.02 a share.
In the 1996 first quarter it reported net income of $552,000, or $0.09 a share, on sales of $6.3 million.
Check Technology, which makes and markets advanced print production systems for financial and forms printers worldwide, said it projected lower first quarter earnings due to soft hardware sales.
Check Technology also said acceptance testing of its Imaggia print production system with beta test partner Liberty Check Printers showed the need for further print module performance refinements.
Delphax Corp, the print module's designer and manufacturer, is evaluating the necessary upgrades and has not yet provided a completion time line, Check Technology said.
It said it would issue an announcement when beta testing begins. Beta testing was previously delayed in July 1996.
A Check Technology spokesman was not available for comment.
As a result of the delay in the commercial launch of Immagia, Check Technology said it is implementing a plan to maximize revenue from its current product line.

That plan includes pursuing sales in Latin America through an increased sales force, marketing alternative applications for its core technology, and continuing to pursue market potential in China and India.

"Despite the delay, Check Technology has made tremendous progress and we eagerly look forward to the benefits the Immagia system will bring to our operation," Michael Provenzano, executive vice president of Liberty Check Printers, said in a statement.
